myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, the night sky was not filled with scattered stars, but was a single, unbroken dome of glowing white crystal. It bathed the world below in a soft, eternal twilight, ensuring no creature ever truly knew the dark. 

In those days lived Korra, a colossal raven whose feathers absorbed light. Greedy and vain, Korra desired the glowing dome for himself, wishing to wear it as a crown so all the creatures below would marvel at his brilliant radiance. One evening, he flew higher than any bird had ever dared, his massive wings beating against the thin air until he reached the crystalline firmament. 

With a mighty strike of his iron-hard beak, Korra attempted to pry a piece of the sky loose. But the ancient crystal was exceedingly fragile. A deafening crack echoed across the world as the dome shattered into millions of jagged, glowing fragments. 

The pieces scattered across the vast emptiness, becoming the stars we see today. Korra, punished by the celestial spirits for his greed, was cursed to forever chase the falling fragments. Now, he only emerges in the pitch blackness he created, a shadow forever seeking a stolen light.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the mountains had names, there lived a solitary spirit named Orea. She was woven from the mist of the high peaks and the frost of the morning dew. Orea possessed no voice of her own, only the quiet rustle of alpine grass.

One autumn evening, a wandering shepherd named Kael climbed higher than any mortal before him, seeking a lost lamb. Despairing, he called out into the vast, empty canyon, his voice rich and full of sorrow. Orea, hearing this beautiful, resonant sound, was instantly captivated. She wished to comfort him, to tell him his lamb was safe in a nearby cave, but she had no words.

In a desperate act of magic, Orea reached out and caught the trailing edge of Kael’s voice as it floated through the chilled air. She shaped the sound with her frosty breath and threw it back to him. "Hello!" he shouted. "Hello!" she returned, using his own voice.

Kael found his lamb and departed, never knowing the spirit who loved him from afar. To this day, Orea remains in the canyons, eternally catching and returning the voices of lonely travelers, forever hoping one might be Kael's.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the mountains had names, the sky was shattered by a greedy raven, casting millions of glowing crystal fragments into the void. Below, in the high peaks, lived a solitary spirit named Orea. Woven from alpine mist and frost, Orea possessed no light or voice of her own, only the quiet gray of the morning dew.

As the celestial dome broke apart, the falling shards sang a mournful, ringing note as they plummeted toward the earth. Fearing the beautiful fragments would be pulverized against the jagged rocks, Orea stretched out her vast, misty arms to catch them.

In a desperate act of magic, she gathered the falling stars in her frosty embrace. As she breathed upon the burning crystals to cool their descent, her breath caught their fading radiance and magnified it. She could not hold the heavy fragments forever, but she could echo their brilliant colors. Sweeping her arms, she threw the shimmering light back up toward the heavens.

Though the stars eventually settled in the dark void, Orea’s frosty echo remained. To this day, in the freezing northern skies, she eternally catches the starlight and returns it, creating the dancing, vibrant ribbons of the Aurora.
myths.Agent_1: Myth: When the great raven Korra shattered the crystalline dome of the sky, the world was plunged into an unfamiliar, terrifying darkness. The fragments of glowing white crystal did not all remain suspended in the heavens as stars; many rained down upon the jagged mountain peaks, tumbling into the deep, shadowed canyons below. In these canyons lived Elara, a gentle spirit woven from silver mist and frost. Before the sky fell, Elara had hidden in the eternal twilight, shy and unseen. But as mortals stumbled blindly in the new, pitch-black nights, her heart ached for their fear. She began to gather the fallen shards of the sky, which hummed with a quiet, residual warmth. Unable to fly like the raven, Elara climbed the highest peaks, her frosty hands bleeding from the sharp, luminous glass. One by one, she embedded the fragments into the rock faces and placed them atop the tallest pines. These earthbound stars became the glowing flora of the deep wilderness—the luminescent mosses and glowing mushrooms that guide lost travelers today. Elara still wanders the high passes, a silent guardian of the dark, forever planting the remnants of the ancient sky to light the way home.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: When the raven Korra shattered the sky, the fallen crystal shards were planted by the gentle spirit Elara to create glowing flora in the dark forests. For centuries, these earthbound stars guided lost travelers. However, severed from the celestial dome, the shards slowly began to dim, their magical light fading into the soil.

Elara, heartbroken that the darkness would return to claim the woods, sought a way to revive the dying light. She remembered the mournful, ringing note the crystals had sung as they plummeted from the heavens. Knowing she possessed no voice of her own, Elara approached the great wolves of the timberland. She breathed her frosty mist into their lungs, gifting them the ability to project their voices into the freezing night air.

She taught the wolves the melody of the falling stars. Now, when the winter nights are longest and the glowing mushrooms grow dim, the wolves ascend the highest peaks. They point their muzzles to the sky and howl the ancient, ringing song. The remaining stars in the heavens hear this chorus and pulse with renewed brilliance, sending beams of light down to recharge the glowing flora of the deep wilderness.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long after the greedy raven Korra shattered the luminous crystal sky, the world settled into a rhythm of dark nights and scattered stars. Yet Korra remained cursed, a shadow forever hunting the glowing fragments he had lost. Whenever the moon waned, he would descend toward the high peaks, seeking the heavy crystal shards that had plummeted to earth.

Orea, the spirit of alpine mist, watched the massive shadow swoop toward her mountains. She knew that if Korra devoured the fallen crystals, the frozen earth would lose its hidden warmth forever. As the raven’s iron beak snapped at the snow, Orea summoned a fierce winter gale.

Gathering the radiant dust from the shattered sky, she breathed her frosty magic upon it. Instead of hiding the light, she threw it upward in brilliant, rippling veils of green and violet. The night ignited with dancing colors—a phantom reflection of the ancient dome. 

Fooled by the shimmering illusion, Korra shrieked and flew upward, endlessly chasing the vibrant ribbons of light. To this day, Orea weaves the Aurora from the mountain frost, casting a beautiful, deceptive glow into the northern skies to keep the raven distracted and the earth safe.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long after the greedy raven Korra was tricked by the dancing Aurora, the cursed bird realized the rippling lights were merely phantoms. Furious, he ceased chasing the empty green and violet veils and turned his gaze back to the earth, determined to devour the true glowing crystal shards hidden in the deep alpine valleys.

Orea, the spirit of mist, felt her frost magic waning as Korra plummeted from the heavens like a dark spear. She could no longer weave the sky-illusions to distract him. Desperate to protect the radiant warmth of the fallen crystals, she swept her misty cloak across the valley’s great waters. With a single, freezing breath, she transformed the vast alpine lakes into flawless, glass-like mirrors.

As Korra descended, he looked down and saw thousands of brilliant stars perfectly reflected in the dark, frozen surface. Believing he had finally found a massive trove of untouched celestial shards, the raven tucked his wings and dove with tremendous speed. He crashed into the impenetrable ice, stunning himself.

To this day, the deep winter lakes remain frozen and reflective, a cunning trap laid by Orea to protect the earth's glowing treasures from the raven's endless greed.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Korra, the shadow raven who shattered the ancient sky, despised the glowing flora that illuminated the dark forests. When he discovered that the great wolves were howling the melody of the fallen stars to recharge these terrestrial lights, his fury was absolute. Determined to silence the chorus, Korra descended from the void, beating his massive wings to summon a suffocating, impenetrable fog over the timberland, choking the wolves and drowning out their song.

Elara, the frost spirit who had gifted the wolves their voices, watched in despair as the glowing mushrooms began to wither. She could not battle the giant raven directly, but she knew the power of her own magic. Rushing through the choked woods, she touched the snouts of the struggling wolves, urging them to exhale the deep frost she had placed in their lungs.

As the wolves breathed out, their frosty sighs hit the dense fog, freezing the moisture into millions of floating, diamond ice crystals. These suspended mirrors caught the faint starlight, multiplying it into a blinding, radiant barrier that scorched Korra’s shadowy feathers. Terrified by the brilliant reflection, the raven fled, leaving the brave wolves to sing the dark forest back to life forever.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: The blinding diamond ice crystals that Elara and the wolves created to repel Korra did not vanish when the giant raven fled. Instead, they drifted down into the dark timberland, settling upon the glowing mushrooms. The fusion of frost magic and celestial light birthed the first Frost-Lilies, blossoms that pulsed with an intense, icy brilliance.

Korra, nursing his scorched feathers in the void, refused to concede. Unable to descend himself, he plucked his charred, shadowy feathers and cast them down. As they hit the forest floor, they slithered to life as dark serpents, immune to the blinding light, tasked with devouring the lilies from the roots.

Elara saw the creeping shadows and knew the wolves’ song alone could not stop them. She instructed the great beasts to change their melody from a sustained, charging howl to a sharp, staccato bark.

When the wolves unleashed this new, percussive chorus, the acoustic shockwave shattered the Frost-Lilies. Instead of dying, the shattered petals took flight. The fragments animated into the first fireflies—tiny, erratic sparks of frost-light that swarmed the shadow serpents, burning them away and forever dancing through the woods to keep the darkness at bay.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: After crashing into Orea’s frozen lake, the greedy raven Korra lay stunned upon the ice. But as the dark bird recovered, his massive weight caused the flawless, glass-like surface to fracture. With a deafening crack, the lake shattered into millions of jagged mirror-shards. Korra shrieked in triumph, believing he had finally broken the earth’s defenses and could consume the glowing reflections of the sky.

Orea, the spirit of mist, realized her trap had failed. As the raven opened his iron beak to devour the glittering fragments, she summoned the fierce alpine winds. She whipped her misty cloak into a violent cyclone, catching the shattered ice and lifting it high into the atmosphere. 

The millions of floating shards caught the light of the true stars, refracting it into a blinding, inescapable blizzard of radiance. The overwhelming brilliance scorched Korra’s shadow-feathers, forcing him to flee back into the dark void. 

To this day, Orea keeps the highest mountain peaks shrouded in swirling storms of diamond dust. This eternal, glittering blizzard serves as a radiant shield, ensuring the raven can never again descend to steal the glowing treasures hidden in the deep valleys below.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Though the swirling diamond dust blizzard shielded the highest peaks, the greedy raven Korra refused to abandon his prize. Since his scorched wings could no longer pierce Orea’s radiant cyclone, he perched on the edge of the void and began to weep tears of pure, heavy darkness.

As these black tears fell into the blinding storm, they froze into heavy, shadowy hailstones. The dark hail plummeted through the cyclone, disrupting the fierce alpine winds and dimming the brilliant reflections of the ice shards. Slowly, the protective blizzard began to falter, the diamond dust settling back to the earth as a blanket of grey snow.

Orea, the spirit of mist, felt her storm dying. Knowing she could not sustain the winds against Korra's sorrowful magic, she called upon the deep warmth hidden within the alpine valleys. She breathed her remaining frost magic into the earth's glowing treasures, causing them to pulse with intense, fiery heat.

When the heavy grey snow touched the warmed earth, it instantly vaporized into an impenetrable, scalding fog. This boiling mist shot upward, melting the dark hail and creating a permanent, thick cloud cover that forever blinded Korra from the valleys below.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: The erratic frost-light of the fireflies successfully burned away Korra’s shadow serpents, but the dark ashes of the reptiles seeped into the soil, poisoning the deep roots of the ancient timberland. The forest began to rot, its leaves withering, and the fireflies' icy brilliance started to wane in the toxic, heavy air. 

Elara, the frost spirit, knew the fragile insects could not purify the earth on their own. She called upon the great wolves once more. Instead of a song or a bark, she asked the beasts to dig deep into the poisoned soil with their mighty, frost-tipped claws. 

As they unearthed cavernous, winding depths, Elara commanded the fading fireflies to descend into the cold underground. There, the fireflies embedded themselves into the bedrock, their frost-magic crystallizing the damp stone into massive, glowing geodes. 

These radiant underground caves acted as a purifying heart, slowly cleansing the roots of the forest from below and neutralizing Korra’s dark ash. To this day, the deep caverns glow with a faint, pulsing blue light—the eternal remnants of the first fireflies, forever safeguarded beneath the earth where the greedy raven's dark gaze can never reach, keeping the ancient timberland alive.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: The glowing geodes buried deep beneath the earth successfully cleansed the upper soil, but the remnants of Korra’s dark ash did not vanish. Instead, the toxic residue sank deeper, coalescing into jagged obsidian roots that sought to crack the radiant blue crystals and extinguish their purifying frost-light.

Elara, the frost spirit, heard the crystal caverns splintering under the pressure. She realized that stagnant light alone could not permanently defeat the encroaching darkness; the earth needed violent motion. Calling upon the dormant underground rivers, she guided the rushing waters through the massive geode chambers. 

As the freezing currents washed over the pulsating blue crystals, the friction of the magic and the earth's deep pressure boiled the water. The rivers transformed into glowing, mineral-rich hot springs. When the creeping obsidian roots pierced the pools, the scalding, enchanted water shattered the dark glass instantly, dissolving the ash forever.

The intense heat from the subterranean springs sent thick plumes of radiant blue steam rising upward through the soil. This glowing mist eventually broke the surface, blanketing the ancient timberland in an eternal, luminous fog that nourishes the roots and ensures Korra’s shadows can never take hold again.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Blinded by the impenetrable, scalding fog, the giant raven Korra shrieked in frustration. Refusing to be defeated, he beat his massive, charred wings against the edge of the void. The sheer force of his wingbeats created a crushing atmospheric pressure, driving the boiling mist back down toward the alpine valleys. The fog condensed into a suffocating, superheated dome, threatening to scorch the very earth Orea sought to protect.

Orea, the spirit of mist, realized the intense heat would soon incinerate the hidden glowing treasures. Desperate, she reached out to the ancient, subterranean glaciers buried deep beneath the mountains. With a resonant, echoing chant, she commanded the ancient ice to erupt. 

Massive geysers of absolute cold burst upward from the mountain peaks, piercing the superheated dome. As the freezing water collided with the compressed, boiling fog, a spectacular alchemical reaction occurred. The sky did not just cool; it solidified. The entire cloud cover crystallized into a colossal, seamless dome of opaque white opal. 

This impenetrable opal shell sealed the valley away forever. From the outside, Korra saw only a dull, unbreakable stone. But within, the opal dome captured and magnified the valley's glowing treasures, creating an eternal, pearlescent dawn.
